name: kolmanskop
ritual: Comment what you think is still buried in the sand

slides.text: Namibia, 1908. A railway worker named Zacharias Lewala was clearing sand off the tracks when he spotted a shiny stone.
It was a diamond. Within a few years, a German mining town rose out of the desert: Kolmanskop.
Stone houses. A ballroom, a casino, a theatre, an ice factory... in the middle of the Namib Desert.
Its hospital had the first X-ray machine in the southern hemisphere. Some say it was used to check workers for swallowed diamonds.
Around 1910, it was one of the richest towns in Africa.
Then bigger diamonds were found further south. People packed up and left, many leaving their things behind.
By 1956, Kolmanskop was empty. And the dunes moved in.
Today, visitors walk through houses filled to the windows with sand.
